decisions.reason: Changing the ESP32 SPI MOSI assignment from GPIO26 to GPIO33 does not alter the defined interboard signal connector or its SDA0, SCL0, IRQ, PWRON, USB, and 5V_EN pinout.
The MOSI GPIO reassignment does not change I2C cable length, speed, pull-ups, or series-resistor conditioning.
The SPI MOSI GPIO assignment is independent of the interboard power connector and its matching pin-order rule.
The source decision changes SPI MOSI only and does not alter the native USB D+ and D- data-line requirement.
An individual ESP32-S3 GPIO reassignment does not change the three-board architecture or the roles of the main and sensor boards.
The SPI MOSI reassignment does not change the standalone USB power source, activation condition, powered rail, loads, or source-selection behavior.
The candidate state defines LED supply, level shifting, and GPIO5-controlled rail shutdown but no SPI MOSI or GPIO26 dependency.
The switched 5V rail already uses GPIO5 for enable control and is unaffected by moving SPI MOSI from GPIO26 to GPIO33.
The source decision does not change the sensor board's role as a connector hub.

The candidate still assigns touch wake to GPIO26, while the supporting source says GPIO26 is unavailable. The client selected GPIO33 specifically for SPI MOSI, but did not decide how the touch-wake assignment should be remapped, so propagation requires a new client decision.
The SPI MOSI reassignment does not change the requirement for an eight-addressable-LED board.
The source decision changes an ESP32 SPI GPIO assignment and does not alter the AXP2101 power source, system rails, or battery power path.
